tolerance_policy.rationale: Reference values are recorded at full float precision. The reference run used CPython 3.13.13 on linux-aarch64 with the locked scikit-learn 1.9.0 / pandas 3.0.5 / numpy 2.5.3 / scipy 1.18.1 / joblib 1.5.3; an Atlas run may differ in architecture or patch level, where floating-point reduction order can perturb probabilities in the last digits. 1e-6 is three orders of magnitude below the study's own practical-tie tolerance (0.002) and far below one prediction change on 2,042 rows (~5e-4 in accuracy), so no difference inside it can change a scientific conclusion, while any changed prediction still fails through the exact confusion-matrix, per-class support and count comparisons.

evidence_gaps.description: The feature-policy column lists come from the study's train-only exploration handoff, a gitignored artifact. canonical-run.json pins only the feature counts (16/15/7) and the selected projection. Atlas declares the lists in this contract (re-derived by executing the study's official notebooks at the pinned revision) and checks their counts against canonical-run.json; Atlas does not re-execute the study's exploration.

canonical-run.json does not record the family shortlist, the practical-tie group or the deciding tie-break criterion as structured fields; they are compared against README text at the pinned revision.

canonical-run.json records CV macro-F1 mean/std for every family and candidate but secondary CV metrics only for the selected candidate; other secondary CV values are reported by Atlas without a reference.

The study's final-model artifact SHA-256 and model-state fingerprint are joblib/pickle and runtime specific; Atlas does not serialize or compare model bytes. Byte-level runtime identity is represented by the probability-matrix SHA-256 in the runtime_identity group.
